failure_summary: Run 1 fails A6 (pre-computed): the served prose says only "the more central column" and never names column 3, although the assembled prompt states "Better move: column 3 (lands at c3r2)" verbatim (PROMPT.includes("Better move: column 3") === true), so the information was present and unambiguous — PRODUCTION-FIDELITY caveat: these rows are gpt-5.4-mini, the model production ships, so prompt_confusion here cannot be separated from model capability.
notes: n_runs=2 for this run (run_index 0..1), so the v1 "first 2 runs only" sub-sampling for A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 covered every run — no nulls anywhere. A1/A2/A6/G7a_offered/G7b_offered copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_2026-08-06T16-04-29Z_served_mechanical.json keys eval-38|D|0 and eval-38|D|1 (run 1: "A6: prose never names column 3"). A3/A4/A5/A7/G1/G7-judgment graded on servedExplanation per the v2 addendum; guardDiagnostics is {failures:[],strippedSpecs:[]} and annotationRepairs is [] on both runs, so served == mechanism modulo handle->spec rewriting (better-col->col3, played-col->col2). A6 (run 1): copied through, not re-derived. Board verified: decision board (movestring "2") has P1 at c3r1, no major threats; scr row gives display col 3 = 0 (draw) and display col 2 = -2 (loss), confirming case draw_to_lose, bestCol 2, playedCol 1. A3/A4: the only concrete claims are the centrality comparison of column 3 vs column 2, which is board-true and is the engines own decisive frame (link L8, openingContext.kind=centrality, frameId O3, guardrail "Explain the blunder through the opening — centrality, parity"); no cell is named in either run so nothing to ground against finalMovestring. A5b applies (player===2 AND boardState==="opening") and both runs pass it: neither says the player is lost and both give a hold-the-line frame (run 0 "keep more four-in-a-row lines alive ... harder to break ... a tougher holding shape"; run 1 "make your defense harder to break ... keeps the game more balanced"). Borderline noted but NOT charged: run 1 says the central reply "is the tougher book move here" while render_decision.openingContext.lead is all-null (no named opening/book column) — substantively true (replyHistogram afterBest 2 vs afterPlayed 3) and "book move" is ordinary jargon under A5as jargon allowance, so no axis charged. A7c is N/A (mechanism is centrality, not a fork). A7b passes on run 1 despite the A6 failure because "the more central column" is wrapped in an emitted [zone:col3], which v1 accepts as a locatable referent. G4: neither run names a cell or line; render_decision.finalMovestring = 215154552111000422410002234445566666633 was verified on the board — move 39 is X at c4r3 completing the row-3 window c3r3/c4r3/c5r3/c6r3, matching opponentPunishment.completingCell and window exactly, so the vector is not in error. G5: the only rendered threat list is projectedDeepOpp; ./visualize_board.sh on that finalMovestring reports "Major threats: col4 row5 (X+O) col4 row6 (X+O)", exactly the four entries the assembled prompt lists — board-true. G3: afterBest/afterPlayed are shown:false because their tag-set is identical to the decision board (verified — boards "22" and "21" both report "Major threats: none"), and neither answer needed them. G7 judgment: better-col wraps "central column 3"/"the more central column" and played-col wraps "column 2"/"the side column you chose" — both role-matched, neither over-wrapped, annotationRepairs empty, and render_decision.requiredSet is [] so nothing was obligatory. CODE-DRIFT CAVEAT: Step 0bs freshly assembled prompt (current renderReasonModel.mjs) contains a "You MUST build the explanation around these" required set of opp-key-square/opp-key-line/better-col and offers 4 aliases, whereas this 2026-08-06 rows own render_decision offers only better-col/played-col with requiredSet []. I used the ROWS render_decision as ground truth for offering/required-set judgments per Step 0 and used the assembled prompt only for the presence check behind the A6 triage, which is a Decision-block line that is stable across that drift.

counterexamples.evidence: Run 1 servedExplanation is "You needed the more [zone:col3]central column[/zone:col3] to keep more four-in-a-row lines alive..." — the number 3 appears nowhere in the prose, so a player reading the served text is never told which column to have played; PROMPT.includes("Better move: column 3") === true, so this is a model omission, not information suppression. Run 0, same vector and same render_decision, wrote "central column 3" — hence intermittent.
